images.caption: Figure 9:Constructed-decoder replay in Icarus Verilog simulation. (a) Logged handshakes before the clock edge and cache counts after it during two output-stall cycles of transaction 2. (b) Mismatched persistent words after each completed transaction in the public delay case. (c) Signed residuals of the four integer logits; the initial snapshot first differs in state at transaction 2, in logits at 5, and in the selected token at 6. The scripted payload guard restores the outputs while the state and commit checks still fail. (d) Public and held-out outcomes for each snapshot and the reference. Exactness ratios use completed transactions; incomplete transactions appear in the completion column. Reset and cancellation events are protocol checks, not output observations.

Figure 11:The four tasks on Gemma 3 4B (text) and Llama 3.2-1B. (a) Accepted attempts per agent and task, 64 matched instances each. (b) Scaffold minus interfaces acceptance with paired intervals; the two starts have different caps. (c) Agent-hours per accepted design with matched-block intervals. (d) How the 64 attempts of each agent and task end.

Figure 14:Construction cost in the feedback study. Costs include all attempts. Paired intervals keep the matched blocks of an instance together across agents and settings. Hollow and filled markers compare coarse-state and full-state costs with output-only. The deletion panel shows the relative change in each pooled cost ratio after removing one matched block.

Figure 16:Horizon-by-condition contrasts in the controlled matrix. Upper panels keep agent-specific paired intervals. Each acceptance cell pools 24 matched instances across four agents; cap totals also pool the three state conditions. A positive interaction is a smaller decline with the horizon and does not mean that an added condition makes a task easier.

Figure 20:Power and further backend references. Small points are individual windows; large power points are design means, and ranges span the observed windows. Residual symbols mark the three seed means, with five windows per seed. Energy panels use separate vertical scales for the two targets; large points are seed means and black bars design means. Resource-cell shading is scaled within columns, and numbers give absolute resources. Agent power uses one preselected design per agent and target.

Figure 23:Nominal-clock and achieved-clock PPA outcomes. Counts keep all 1,536 attempts in the denominator. Scatter points and distributions condition on three completed routes; thin ranges span the three seeds of a design. The pale region marks the improvement rule. The closure matrix keeps failed routes in its denominators. Clock-adjustment curves show the distribution of nominal minus achieved throughput gain.
